sentences.text: 2. MFA No.8250/2012 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 19.08.2010 at about 10.30 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-ET- 3289 as a pillion rider on NH-4,
Kolar-Bangalore Road near MVG Hospital, at that time a lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-29- U-8045 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore, the claimant preferred claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act, seeking compensation.

4. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
5.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that in the present case, considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, certainly, he would have been riding the motorcycle but not as the pillion rider but by falsely stating that the claimant was pillion rider.
Hence, filed claim petition so as to make claim against the Insurance Company.
Therefore, it is submitted that on all its preponderance of probabilities of sustaining injuries, the claimant was riding motorcycle but not as the pillion rider.
Therefore, prays to set-aside the finding given by the Tribunal that the claimant as a pillion rider and sustained injuries.

6. Further, it is submitted that the doctor has stated the permanent physical disability of 14% but the Tribunal has taken 100% functional disability which is on the higher side and an exaggerated one.

Therefore, it is submitted that even in the case of amputation of leg as per Schedule II of the Employee's Compensation Act,1923 maximum 60% of permanent physical disability is to be considered but not 100% in the case like of claimant.
Therefore, prays to reduce the quantum of compensation by allowing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company holding that the claimant was rider of the motorcycle but not as the pillion rider.
Hence, the claim is not maintainable and also on quantum, alternatively, it is the submission that to reduce the quantum of compensation.
7. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the claimant was pillion rider and that is reflected in the complaint which is filed at an earliest point of time.
Therefore, it is proved that the claimant was a pillion rider.
Just because the rider has not sustained injuries and the claimant being pillion rider, has sustained injuries that does not mean that the claimant was rider of the motorcycle.

Therefore, it is submitted that by nature of injuries sustained, it cannot be held that whether the claimant was rider of the motorcycle or not but the fact remains that the claimant has sustained injuries.

Further, it is submitted that the Tribunal has taken functional disability at 100% is correct considering the claimant is a coolie by profession but the notional income held by the Tribunal is lower side.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of the compensation and to dismiss the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: In the present case, the claimant had sustained fracture of tibia, femur, patella of left leg and also sustained fracture of right clavicle and also it is proved from the medical evidence that the claimant had suffered amputation of left leg below the knee.
Upon perusing the complaint which is given on the next day of the accident, it is mentioned that the claimant was pillion rider on the motorcycle.
Admittedly, the rider had sustained simple injuries.

It is argument canvassed by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that considering the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, it proves that the claimant was riding the motorcycle but not as a pillion rider.

Therefore, on the basis of nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, it is the submission of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the claimant definitely would have been riding the motorcycle but not as a pillion rider.
Considering this submission and evidence on record, in the complaint Ex.P1 which is given on 20.08.2010 on the next day of the accident by mentioning that the claimant was a pillion rider.
The accident is an accident.
It cannot be expected how many injuries are occurred to the rider and pillion rider and what are the nature of injuries.
Just because the rider had not sustained grievous injuries that does not mean that the rider was not riding the motorcycle.

In accident,
anything may be happened including nature of injuries.
In accident, one may sustain simple injuries and other may sustain grievous as in the present case.
Therefore, in the accident, it cannot be expected such and such nature of injuries are only occurred and not otherwise.
Therefore, when the evidence on record proves that the claimant had suffered injuries as above stated, there is no merit found in the contentions urged by the Insurance Company.
Therefore, in this regard, the Tribunal has given correct finding.
Upon perusing the police documentary evidence, it is proved that the claimant was pillion rider and had sustained injuries.

sentences.text: In the present case, the claimant had sustained fracture of tibia, femur, patella of left leg and also sustained fracture of right clavicle.
The medical evidence on record also proves that amputation of below the knee was conducted.
The claimant is a coolie by profession.
Therefore, the compensation of Rs.50,000/- awarded under the head 'pain and agony' is on the lesser side.
Therefore, the same is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
11. Further, the compensation granted under the head 'medical expenses and hospital charges' is as per the actual medical bills produced before the Tribunal by the claimant.
Therefore, the same is kept in tact.
12. The Tribunal has assessed the functional disability at 100%.

The doctor had stated that the claimant had suffered 66% of disability towards left lower limb and 24.6% towards left femur and the fractured leg is - 11 - not united and having become infected and having sustained infection.
The aspect of physical disability and functional disability are two different.
The doctors can say only regarding physical disability whether it is permanent partial disability or permanent total disability.
But the functional disability is to be assessed considering the nature of injuries and disability sustained and nature of avocation, etc.
In this regard, I place reliance on the following judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of -  Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

sentences.text: Therefore, as per the principle of law laid down by the Supreme Court in the above said judgments, the present case is one that considering the functional disability as 100% considering the claimant being coolie by profession.
The work of coolie requires much physical strength.

Therefore,
amputation of one leg, work of coolie cannot be performed amounting to 100% functional disability which is correctly held by the Tribunal.
Therefore, on this aspect there is no need to make any interference in this regard.
14. Since the claimant had suffered 100% functional disability, it amounts to 'loss of future prospects in life' considering the claimant had suffered amputation of left leg.

Therefore, certain amount is added towards 'loss of future prospects in life' as per the decision of the division bench of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Ltd., Vs. sentences.text: Accordingly, the claimant being 34 years old, 40% of income is to be added towards 'loss of future prospects in life'.
The accident was occurred in the year 2010.
Therefore, the notional income would be Rs.5,500/- as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As the claimant was aged 34 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '16'.

Hence, 'loss of earning capacity due to disability' is hereby re-assessed and quantified as under:
Rs.5,500 + Rs.2,200 (40% of Rs.5,500) = Rs.7,700/- Rs.7,700 x 16 x 12 =
Rs.14,78,400/-
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.14,78,400/- is awarded under the head 'loss of earning capacity due to disability'.
15. Further, the compensation of Rs.33,000/- (Rs.5,500 x 6 months) is awarded under the head 'loss of - 14 - income during laid up period' by holding monthly income of Rs.5,500/- for six months.
16. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head 'loss of amenities and unhappiness' which is on the lesser side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
For incidental expenses like food, nourishment, conveyance, attendant charges, etc., the Tribunal has not awarded the compensation.
Hence, a sum of Rs.40,000/- awarded under the said head.
17. The compensation of Rs.25,000/- granted under the head 'future medical expenses' is on the lesser side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.

18. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following sums:

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.9,96,400/- (Rs.18,91,400 - Rs.8,95,000) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
20.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The MFA No.8560/2012 filed by the claimant is allowed-in-part.
Consequently, the MFA No.8250/2012 filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.

The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.7414/2010 is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.9,96,400/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal, forthwith.
iv. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records along with certified copy of this order without delay.
v. Costs made easy.
